name: Carrd
tagline: Simple, responsive one-page websites for almost anything
team: Solo founder; 2-person team by 2021, later reported as ~4
summary: Carrd is a builder for single-page websites such as personal profiles, landing pages and link-in-bio pages. It has a free tier and cheap annual Pro plans. AJ, a pseudonymous developer, built it alone, reached $1M ARR with 2.5M sites by April 2021, and took a small funding round. Indie Hackers later reported it at about $2M ARR.
origin: AJ was already known for free HTML site templates and had a Twitter following from that work. He ran a beta of Carrd in late 2015 and launched it publicly in March 2016 as 'a free platform for building simple, fully responsive one-page sites for pretty much anything', getting early traction from his existing followers and Product Hunt.
howItMakesMoney: Freemium, billed annually only: Pro Lite $9/yr, Pro Standard $19/yr and Pro Plus $49/yr. Higher tiers unlock custom domains, forms, embeds and more sites. The very low annual price turns a large free user base into a steady stream of small payments.
growth: Word of mouth and 'Made with Carrd' branding on free sites act as built-in distribution.
Adopted by creators, fandom communities and link-in-bio users, a segment larger site builders ignored.
Seasonal sales (Oct to Dec 2017, Mar 2018) gave clear revenue bumps, which AJ shared in public stats.
Deliberately limited features, keeping the product simple rather than chasing full website-builder parity.
Zero paid marketing: Indie Hackers reported ~$2M ARR in 2024 with a small team and no ad budget.
moat: A very low price anchor ($19/yr) combined with millions of sites and strong brand affinity among young creators makes it hard for competitors to undercut or out-simplify.
risks: Link-in-bio and AI site generators compete for the same simple-site use case. The low price leaves little room if hosting or support costs rise.

timeline.event: Private beta; some beta users still pay years later
AJ publishes monthly users, sites and revenue stats for Jan 2016 to Apr 2018
Announces 2.5M sites, $1M ARR and a funding round
Indie Hackers reports Carrd at ~$2M ARR with a small team and no ad spend

lessons: A tiny annual price can beat monthly SaaS pricing when the free tier is huge and the upgrade is obvious.
Feature restraint is a positioning choice: 'simple one-page' is the product.
An audience from earlier free work (templates) can seed a paid product's launch.
Free-tier branding compounds as a zero-cost acquisition channel.

rebuild.idea: A one-page site builder just for local tradespeople (plumbers, electricians, cleaners) with built-in quote-request forms, service-area maps and Google review embeds, at $29/yr.
rebuild.why: General builders force tradespeople through design choices they don't care about. Most need one page that ranks locally and collects quote requests.
mvp: Build 3 templates with a quote form that emails and texts the owner.
Hand-build 10 sites for tradespeople found through Google Maps listings that have no website.
Add 'Built with ...' branding to every free site.
rebuild.fit: Front-end developers who can do local outreach
